body.estimand_functional: With probability tending to one, \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\); the upper bound is attained by the graph-selected one-shot seed procedure with its branch-safe fallback, while equality with the lower scale remains unresolved.

sampling_model.design: The graph \(G=G_n\) is revealed first.  On \(M_n<n\), the experimenter fixes \(c_0\in(0,1)\), computes the robust candidate \(\widetilde k_n=\max\{1,\lfloor c_0/[-\log(1-M_n/n)]\rfloor\}\) and the log-tuned candidate \(k_n^\sharp=\max\{1,\lfloor\log(d_n+1)/[4\{-\log(1-M_n/n)\}]\rfloor\}\), and chooses the candidate with smaller graph certificate before drawing seeds.  It then treats the union of the selected number of uniform seeds' closed neighborhoods.  The finite fallback assigns every unit treatment when the positive-exposure branch is unavailable or the selected certificate exceeds one.
sampling_model.units: The population \(V_n\) and every potential outcome are fixed conditional on \(G\). The graph is random only for the high-probability frontier statement.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one binary assignment \(Z\) is drawn and all realized outcomes are observed. Seed multiplicities are integrated out of the estimator by conditional Rao--Blackwell weights.
sampling_model.overlap: No unit-level Bernoulli overlap is imposed. The seed branch is entered only when \(M_n<n\), where all endpoint exposure probabilities used in ratios are graph-computable and positive. When \(M_n\ge n\), the compiler forms no inverse-probability quantity and returns the all-treated fallback.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Intermediate-exposure potential outcomes are unrestricted and ignored; no prior outcomes, repeated rounds, endpoint means, behavioral model, or superpopulation outcome law is used.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Corollary 5.4 gives \(d/n\lesssim\mathcal R(G,\tau_{\mathrm{GATE}},2)\lesssim d^2/n\) with high probability for random \(d\)-regular \(G\) and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).
Theorem 4.1 bounds the modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by \(12.5\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) times the sum of endpoint empirical second moments.
Algorithm 4 is the paper's polynomial approximation design, Proposition 4.3 states its guarantee, and Theorem C.11 is the imported 2-approximation for Partial Vertex Cover used as a subroutine.
Theorem 4.8 bounds GATE Horvitz--Thompson variance for randomized one-hop-max clustering under bounded outcomes and restricted growth.
The paper characterizes admissible estimable quadratic variance bounds and gives convex programs selecting minimally conservative bounds for linear estimators.

body.tldr: For a revealed uniform simple \(d_n\)-regular network under unrestricted arbitrary neighborhood interference and endpoint empirical second-moment bounds, the proved result is the high-probability bracket \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\).  The lower side is design-uniform.  For the upper side, a one-shot neighborhood-seed design selects the better graph certificate from a fixed-exponent robust count and a log-tuned count; the robust candidate needs only the deterministic row-sum bound.  The selected procedure gives finite conditional coverage and unconditional radius \(O(d_n/\sqrt{\alpha n})=o(1)\) for fixed \(\alpha\).  Its sharper logarithmic radius is conditional on an unresolved Boolean radius-two operator conjecture; no matched minimax order or strict upper-scale improvement is claimed.

project_justification.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4, leaves \(d_n/n\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\) for the same random-regular full-GATE problem.  The present result raises the all-procedure lower edge to \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), reducing the polynomial factor-\(d_n\) gap to a logarithmic gap while retaining the published upper order.
project_justification.niche: Balanced simultaneous endpoint exposure supplies a two-arm Bayes converse, while certificate-based selection between fixed-exponent and log-tuned neighborhood-seed counts makes the exact Schur construction robust without discarding a possible sharper rate.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the balanced-packing lower scale, constructs an observed-data Rao--Blackwell seed estimator, and includes a fixed-exponent candidate for which the elementary bound \(\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le d_n^2+1\) yields the uniform \(d_n^2/n\) upper scale.  The graph chooses the smaller of this certificate and the log-tuned certificate before assignment.  A branch-safe compiler and a Markov risk interval provide finite-sample inference; the remaining logarithmic improvement is isolated as a conjecture rather than assumed.

body.related_work: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, arXiv:2608.04909v1, Corollary 5.4 and Appendix E.4, is the closest comparator: it places the same random-regular full-GATE risk between \(d_n/n\) and \(d_n^2/n\).  The present balanced-exposure converse improves its lower edge to \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) but retains its upper order, leaving a logarithmic gap.  Its Algorithm 4 and Proposition 4.3 motivate finite design computation but do not give the graph-selected seed certificate.  KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, arXiv:2411.10908v3, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1, supplies a generic conflict-graph variance scale; the current unconditional upper bound does not strictly improve that scale.  UganderYin2023RGCR studies randomized graph cluster designs under bounded outcomes and a fixed Horvitz--Thompson procedure, rather than unrestricted minimax risk.  AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference supplies the exposure-mapping foundation.  BehagueIlkovicMontgomery2025Sandwich supports the proved random-regular packing transfer in its verified degree regime.  Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Theorems 14--15, treats graph-matrix shapes but does not uniformly resum the unbounded \(K_{2,r}\)-type terms in the Boolean inclusion--exclusion expansion.  BauerschmidtEtAl2020EdgeRigidity and Sarid2023SpectralGap control adjacency spectra, not this Boolean correction.  HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance optimizes conservative bounds for fixed linear estimators and does not choose the minimax design.  ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice remains the prospective application: a larger one-round all-free versus all-fixed random-regular public-goods experiment can use the robust certificate without assuming its behavioral outcomes attain worst-case risk.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For \(i\ne j\), let \(c_{ij}=(A_G^2)_{ij}\).  The exact identity is \(B_2(G)_{ij}=A_{G,ij}+(1-A_{G,ij})\sum_{r=1}^{d_n}(-1)^{r+1}\binom{c_{ij}}r\), with \(B_2(G)_{ii}=1\).  The unresolved conjecture is that some universal \(L<\infty\) satisfies \(\Pr\{\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\}\to1\) uniformly over every admissible degree sequence.  Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Theorems 14--15, does not by itself uniformly resum these unbounded \(K_{2,r}\)-type shapes.  Accordingly the conjecture is not a premise of the unconditional risk or confidence theorem; it yields only the separately labeled logarithmic refinement.
body.honest_scope: The established same-assumption result is a logarithmic minimax bracket, not a matched frontier.  The robust candidate in the graph-selected seed design gives an unconditional \(d_n^2/n\) upper bound on every sufficiently large simple \(d_n\)-regular graph, while the random-regular balanced-packing result gives the high-probability \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) lower bound over all procedures.  The Boolean operator estimate remains an explicit conjecture; if true, the selected design automatically uses a certificate no larger than the log-tuned one.  Seed probabilities and inverse weights are formed only on \(M_n<n\); the complementary branch uses an all-treated fallback.  The result concerns one assignment, unrestricted intermediate ANI outcomes, and the full population GATE.  It does not cover later strategic feedback, final wealth, two-hop individual payoff, repeated experiments, nonuniform graph draws, or a claim that the ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice behavioral model is worst case.
